predecessors.name: Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia
predecessors.text: the Croat-majority municipalities of Herzegovina and western and central Bosnia (1991 census: 1,238,512 people in the claimed territory, 44.91% Croats)

successors.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
successors.text: the Croat-held land 'to be joined with Bosniaks into the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina' under the Washington Agreement of March 1994

ledger.x: 18 November 1991: the Croatian Community of Herzeg-Bosnia is proclaimed.
28 August 1993: Herzeg-Bosnia is declared a republic.
March 1994: the Washington Agreement ends the Croat-Bosniak war.
March 1994: Herzeg-Bosnia's land is joined to the Federation.

wars.name: Croat-Bosniak War
wars.outcome: Ended by the Washington Agreement of March 1994 (ceasefire 18 March), which joined the Croat-held land with the Bosniak-held land into the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

certainty.note: A claim and a front, not a border: the entity 'never fully controlled' its proclaimed territory; the page lists no municipalities.
